name: Family guesthouses around Dr Zakir Hussain Road, Darjeeling
summary: The lanes above Chowrasta and along Dr Zakir Hussain Road hold dozens of small family-run guesthouses with simple rooms, hot water by bucket or geyser and home-cooked breakfasts. This is where our Budget travellers sleep in Darjeeling.
body: Most of these guesthouses are run by Nepali, Tibetan or Bhutia families in old two- or three-storey houses. Rooms are plain: a double bed, thick quilts, an attached bathroom and sometimes a window facing Kangchenjunga. Breakfast is usually eggs, toast and tea, and many will cook a dal-bhat dinner if you ask in the morning.

The trade-off is the climb. The upper lanes are steep and cars often cannot reach the door, so you carry your bags for the last few minutes. Heating is a plug-in heater at best, which matters from December to February. We pick houses that have a geyser, a working backup for power cuts and owners who answer the phone.
why: Walking distance to Chowrasta, Mall Road and the toy train station
Home-cooked food and real local advice from the owners
Rooms with a mountain view can be had for under ₹2,500
Money stays with Darjeeling families

faqs.q: Do Darjeeling budget guesthouses have heating?
faqs.a: Few have central heating. Most offer a plug-in room heater, sometimes for an extra ₹200–300 a night, plus heavy quilts. From December to February night temperatures in town drop to 1–5°C, so ask about the heater before you book, and pack thermal layers. Rooms on the sunny side of the building are noticeably warmer in the afternoon.

faqs.q: Can a car reach the guesthouse door?
faqs.a: Often not. Many guesthouses sit on narrow, steep lanes above Chowrasta where cars are restricted. Drivers usually drop you at the nearest road point, such as the Gandhi Road side or the Zakir Hussain Road junction, and you walk five to ten minutes. Pack in a bag you can carry uphill, or ask the owner to send someone to help.

faqs.q: Is hot water available all day?
faqs.a: Most guesthouses now have an electric geyser in each bathroom, but some still heat water on request or supply it by bucket. Power cuts happen in the hills, and a geyser is useless without a backup. Ask whether the house has an inverter or generator, and plan showers for the afternoon when the water tank is warmest.

name: Trekkers' lodges and homestays on the Singalila ridge
price_band: ₹400–1,500 per bed or ₹1,500–3,500 per room, meals extra
summary: On the way to Sandakphu you sleep in simple stone and timber lodges at Tumling, Gairibas, Kalipokhri and Sandakphu itself. Expect shared rooms, thick blankets, basic toilets and hot dal-bhat by the kitchen fire.
body: The ridge has a mix of family-run lodges and government trekkers' huts. Family lodges at Tumling and Kalipokhri are the warmest, because you eat in the kitchen next to the stove. At Sandakphu there are several lodges and a government trekkers' hut, and rooms fill early in October, November, April and May.

Facilities are basic. Toilets may be outside, running water can freeze in winter and electricity often comes from solar panels for a few hours. Bring a sleeping-bag liner, a head torch and a power bank. Your licensed guide will normally book lodges ahead; walk-in beds are possible outside peak weeks.
why: The only way to sleep high on the ridge for sunrise views
Hot meals cooked by the families who live there
Prices are low and mostly go to local households
Lodges sit on the classic route, so daily stages stay sensible

faqs.q: Do I need to book Sandakphu lodges in advance?
faqs.a: In October, November and late March to May, yes, because rooms at Sandakphu and Tumling fill with groups. Your licensed guide from Manebhanjan usually phones ahead and confirms. In winter and early spring walk-in beds are easier to find, but lodges may close in heavy snow. Check current status before you travel, especially from December to February.

faqs.q: How cold do the lodges get at night?
faqs.a: Very cold. Sandakphu sits at 3,636 m and night temperatures fall below 0°C from November to March, and to around 5°C even in May. Rooms are unheated. Lodges supply heavy quilts, but bring a sleeping bag rated to about -5°C, a fleece and a warm hat. The kitchen fire is the warmest place in the evening.

faqs.q: What food do the ridge lodges serve?
faqs.a: Simple, hot and filling food: dal-bhat with vegetables, noodles, Maggi, eggs, thukpa, tea and sometimes momos. Menus get shorter and prices rise the higher you go, because supplies come up by Land Rover or porter. A full dinner is usually ₹200–400. Carry snacks such as dry fruit and chocolate for the walking hours between lodges.

name: Sinclairs Siliguri
summary: A long-running mid-range hotel in Siliguri, part of the Kolkata-based Sinclairs chain. We use it when a late train or an early flight forces a night in the plains.
body: Sinclairs is one of the older established hotels in Siliguri, with air-conditioned rooms, a pool and a restaurant that serves Indian, Chinese and continental food. It is well placed for the Hill Cart Road, Sevoke Road and the Darjeeling and Sikkim jeep stands, and NJP station is about a 20-minute drive away.

Siliguri is a transit city, and most travellers only need a clean room, a quiet night and an early start. Sinclairs gives you that with fewer surprises than cheaper station hotels. Book a room on the higher floors away from the road for less traffic noise.
why: Reliable rooms and hot water for a transit night
Easy access to NJP, Bagdogra and the hill roads
Restaurant on site for late arrivals
Air conditioning for hot, humid summer nights in the plains

faqs.q: How far is Sinclairs Siliguri from NJP and Bagdogra?
faqs.a: Allow about 20–30 minutes by taxi to New Jalpaiguri (NJP) station and 30–45 minutes to Bagdogra airport, depending on traffic. Siliguri traffic can be slow between 9 am and 8 pm, especially near Sevoke Road and the Air View More crossing. For a morning flight, leave at least two and a half hours before departure to allow for airport security queues.

faqs.q: Is it worth staying a night in Siliguri?
faqs.a: Only if your timing forces it. Siliguri sits at about 120 m, is hot and humid from April to September, and most sights are on its edges. If your train arrives after about 3 pm, a night in Siliguri is safer than driving the hill road in the dark. Otherwise head straight to Kurseong, Mirik or Darjeeling.

faqs.q: Does Sinclairs Siliguri arrange airport or station transfers?
faqs.a: Most mid-range Siliguri hotels, including this one, can arrange a car to NJP or Bagdogra on request. Prepaid taxis also run from both NJP and the airport. A local transfer within Siliguri is usually ₹400–800 depending on time and distance. Confirm the price with the front desk when you book, and check current rates before you travel.

name: Cochrane Place
summary: A small heritage hotel in an old planter's house just below Kurseong on the Pankhabari road, with tea-garden views and well-kept rooms. Good value for a quiet first or last night in the hills.
body: Cochrane Place is a converted colonial house with an added wing, set among tea gardens below Kurseong. Each room is named and furnished differently, the food is cooked in-house and tea tastings use leaf from neighbouring Darjeeling estates. On clear mornings Kangchenjunga shows above the ridges.

It works well as a soft landing from NJP or Bagdogra, about 1.5–2 hours away, before you go higher to Darjeeling. It is also a good base for Makaibari and Castleton tea estates and the walks around Kurseong. Some rooms are up stairs and steps, so ask for a ground-level room if mobility is a concern.
why: Character rooms in a real planter-era house
Close to Makaibari and the Kurseong tea walks
Quieter and warmer than Darjeeling, at about 1,450 m
Shorter drive from Siliguri for late arrivals

faqs.q: How do I reach Cochrane Place from Siliguri?
faqs.a: The hotel lies on the Pankhabari road below Kurseong, roughly 30 km from Siliguri. A reserved car from NJP or Bagdogra takes about 1.5–2 hours and costs around ₹1,800–2,500. Shared jeeps run to Kurseong town, but the hotel is outside town, so you would still need a local taxi for the last stretch. Ask the hotel to arrange a pickup.

faqs.q: Is Kurseong a good base instead of Darjeeling?
faqs.a: For a quiet stay, yes. Kurseong is lower and warmer, less crowded and close to the tea estates. Darjeeling town is about 32 km and 1.5 hours away, so day trips work, though Tiger Hill sunrise needs a very early start of around 3 am. Many of our travellers split their nights: one in Kurseong, two or three in Darjeeling.

faqs.q: Can I visit tea gardens from Cochrane Place?
faqs.a: Yes. Makaibari and Castleton estates are both within a short drive, and the hotel can suggest guided walks through the gardens and nearby villages. Factory visits depend on the season and the estate's rules, and plucking is busiest from March to November. Check current status before you travel, because estates sometimes close factory visits to the public.

name: Windamere Hotel
price_band: ₹14,000–25,000 per room per night, usually with meals
summary: Darjeeling's best-known heritage hotel, on Observatory Hill a few minutes' walk from Chowrasta. Built as Ada Villa in 1841, it became the Windamere Hotel in 1939 and still keeps its colonial manners.
body: The Windamere sits on Observatory Hill above the Mall, with cottages and rooms spread around old gardens. Rooms have fireplaces or heaters, hot-water bottles appear in the beds at night, and high tea is served in the afternoon. It is quiet, a little old-fashioned on purpose, and very central.

Prices usually include some meals, and the hotel is popular with couples and returning guests, so October and April to May fill early. It is the obvious Comfort-tier choice for travellers who want history and a walkable location over modern design.
why: Real colonial history, from 1841 on Observatory Hill
A two-minute walk to Chowrasta and Mall Road
Fireplaces, warm beds and a quiet garden setting
Afternoon tea in the old lounges

faqs.q: Is the Windamere Hotel worth the price?
faqs.a: If you value history, location and service, it is. You walk to Chowrasta in minutes, the rooms have fireplaces or heaters, and meals are often included in the rate. Rooms are older in style than modern hotels, so if you want contemporary bathrooms and gym facilities, a newer hotel may suit you better at a similar price.

faqs.q: Can cars reach the Windamere Hotel?
faqs.a: Vehicle access to the Mall and Observatory Hill is restricted. Cars usually drop guests at the nearest permitted point and hotel staff help with luggage for the short walk. Tell the hotel your arrival time in advance so someone meets you. This restriction is also what keeps the area around the hotel quiet in the evenings.

faqs.q: When should I book the Windamere?
faqs.a: Book two to three months ahead for October, November, late March to May and the Christmas to New Year week. These are the clear-weather and holiday peaks, and the hotel has a limited number of rooms. Winter from December to February is quieter and cheaper, with the clearest mountain views, but nights are cold.

name: Glenburn Tea Estate
price_band: ₹40,000–60,000 per room per night, all meals and activities included
summary: A working Darjeeling tea estate with a small planter's bungalow guesthouse above the Rungeet river, about 1.5–2 hours' drive from Darjeeling town. It is the splurge stay on our list.
body: Glenburn is a working tea garden whose old bungalows have been turned into a handful of suites. Stays are all-inclusive: meals, guided walks through the tea, factory visits in season and a picnic by the river. The estate sits on a ridge facing Kangchenjunga, well away from Darjeeling traffic.

This is far above our usual prices, and we only suggest it for special trips such as honeymoons or anniversaries. Two nights is the right length. The drive in is slow and partly on estate roads, so arrive in daylight.
why: Sleep on a working tea estate, not a resort
All meals, walks and tea tastings included
Quiet setting with Kangchenjunga views
A small number of rooms, so it never feels crowded

faqs.q: How far is Glenburn from Darjeeling town?
faqs.a: Glenburn lies in the Rangli Rangliot block, roughly 1.5–2 hours' drive from Darjeeling town, with the last part on narrow estate roads. From NJP or Bagdogra allow about 4 hours. The estate normally arranges transfers. It is not a base for daily sightseeing in Darjeeling, so plan your town nights separately and treat Glenburn as a destination in itself.

faqs.q: What does a Glenburn stay include?
faqs.a: Rates are normally all-inclusive: accommodation, all meals, drinks such as estate tea, guided walks through the gardens and, in season, a visit to the tea factory. Some activities like a river picnic depend on weather. Check the current inclusions and minimum stay when you book, because rules and prices can change from season to season.

faqs.q: When is the best time to stay at a Darjeeling tea estate?
faqs.a: March to May is first and second flush, when plucking is active and the factory runs. October and November bring clear skies and autumn tea. Monsoon from June to September is green and quiet but often cloudy, with occasional road disruption. Winter is clear and cold, but tea production usually pauses from December to February.
